units.text: A skill is a ladder: ordered rungs, climbed in advance-set order.
A skill is a rope: many weak crossing strands, none running the whole length.
Ladder-trained skill collapses when the problem turns sideways.
Watch anyone good: splicing, not climbing — short strands joined until the join disappears.
Practice should braid, not stack: two hours across three problems beats six up one.
The objection: ropes cannot be inspected; a ladder shows which rung is missing.
The objection lands: a braid hides its gaps until it is loaded.
Keep both pictures: climb mapped ground, braid unmapped, and know which you are on.
